title: Isochronous prefill buffer gating and threadlet pooling to reduce CPU→GPU jitter
creator: Marco Ortega
description:
Background: We observe intermittent p99 prefill+decode latency spikes attributable to small, frequent CPU→GPU memcpys and threadpool contention on hosts serving mixed short/long sequences. Existing coalescing mitigations reduce average CPU overhead but leave isochronous (burst-aligned) jitter and tail latency intact for real-time workloads.

Goal: Implement a lightweight buffering and scheduling layer that (1) gates prefill writes into isochronous drain windows to reduce memcpy bursts, (2) introduces a 'threadlet' pooled execution model to reduce thread wake/parking churn and NUMA ping-pong, and (3) integrate a kernel-latency predictor hook so the kernel selector can prefer fused attention kernels when beneficial. Target: reduce p99 prefill+first-decode latency by >=20% for mixed workloads and cut memcpy syscall rate by >=40%.

Design summary:
- Isochronous prefill gate: per-GPU ring gate that aggregates small host-side writes and exposes configurable drain windows (e.g., 250–500us). Gate supports dynamic window sizing driven by recent latency/throughput telemetry.
- Single-writer multi-reader staging slab: a small pinned host slab per GPU that accepts aggregated writes; writer enqueues DMA descriptors; multiple readers (GPU-side kernels) can safely read via queued fences. This avoids creating many short-lived pinned buffers.
- Threadlet pooling: a lightweight user-mode thread pool optimized for frequent short tasks (prefill assembly, memcpy descriptor emission). Threadlets are pinned to NUMA domains and reuse per-thread local work queues to avoid global locks. They implement cooperative yielding and a fast-path for polling DMA completion to reduce syscalls.
- Kernel-latency predictor hook: a compact predictor (historical EWMA + small feature vector for seq_len, batch_size, quantization mode) that estimates decode kernel latency and surfaces a boolean to the kernel selector to prefer fused attention or alternate kernel variants.
- Backpressure & adaptive gating: when predicted kernel latency or GPU queue depth exceeds thresholds, the gate increases drain rate to prioritize latency; when underutilized, it favors larger aggregates to improve efficiency.

Why different from prior work: Rather than only coalescing copies or tuning thread counts, this proposal treats the host GPU boundary as an isochronous scheduling domain and couples it with a low-latency threadlet abstraction and kernel-aware signals. The single-writer slab reduces the lifecycle cost of pinned buffers, avoiding repetitive mlock/pin churn seen in traces.

Implementation notes:
- New runtime module: host/io/gate (C++/Rust shim depending on service) + small kernel predictor library in runtime/common.
- Must support fallbacks: if gating disabled, behavior reverts to existing path.
- Expose tuning knobs via config: gate_window_us, slab_size_bytes, threadlet_count_per_numa, predict_window_smoothing, gating_mode (adaptive|static|off).

Acceptance criteria: [list of measurable outcomes]
acceptance_criteria: p99 prefill+first-decode latency reduced by >=20% on mixed short/long sequence benchmark compared to baseline (same hardware)
memcpy syscall rate reduced by >=40% per GPU host on synthetic small-write workload
no regression in throughput for long-sequence workloads (+/-5%)
thread wake/park syscalls measured at host reduced by >=30% during high concurrency tests
feature gated behind runtime flag and safe fallback path exists
tests: bench/mixed_seq_benchmark (short:128, long:2048) run at target QPS for 30 minutes — capture p50/p95/p99 and syscall rates
stress/pinned_slab_lifecycle_test to validate no leaking of pinned pages after repeated open/close of sessions
unit/threadlet_pool_test for queue fairness and NUMA pin correctness
integration/e2e_with_kernel_selector to verify predictor influences kernel choice and fallback correctness
metrics: GPU queue depth and kernel start delay
risks: Incorrect tuning of gate window could increase latency for very small real-time requests — mitigated by adaptive defaults and canary rollout
Pinned slab size misconfiguration could exhaust host locked memory on denser hosts — include safety caps and OOM guards
Threadlet model complexity could hide deadlocks if not carefully instrumented — require aggressive CI and deadlock detectors
Predictor bias might steer to slower kernel variants in rare quantization combos — keep selector telemetry and automatic rollback
dependencies: ENG-112358 (NUMA pinning helpers and thread affinity primitives)
infra/driver-team: kernel DMA fence tracing (internal telemetry)
